title: G7: the daemon writes routine fix rounds itself (gate red with failing test ids, review request_changes with concrete comments) and reconciles the original task's merged_into when the fix round merges; design or scope changes still escalate to the Planner
spec:
Depends on G6 (T-0268, stage leases). Today a held task waits for the Planner to write a fix-round spec by hand (this session wrote six), and after the fix round merges the Planner marks the original done + merged_into by hand. Held tasks already carry hold_reason and resume_hint (tests-green failures text, rebase conflicts), review tasks carry result.comments with path, line, issue, severity, and constraints.fix_round_for makes spawn.base_for cut the fix worktree from the held task's branch.
Change daemon.py:
1. auto_fix_round(task) runs in tick() for held execute tasks with no fix round yet (no task with constraints.fix_round_for == id that is not failed). Routine when: hold_reason is gate_red and resume_hint.failures names at least one FAIL or ERROR test id, or hold_reason starts 'review request_changes' and the review's result.comments all have a path inside the task scope; and the task has had fewer than [daemon].auto_fix_rounds (pool.toml, default 2) automatic rounds. Otherwise (spec_review request_changes, merge conflict, comments outside scope, no concrete failure, rounds exhausted) leave the hold for the Planner and notify once.
2. The fix task: title 'fix round <n>: <original title>', spec rendered from a new .orchestrator/prompts/fix-round.md with the original task id and title, the failed acceptance criteria (those whose text mentions a failing test id, else all), the failure text capped at 3,000 chars, the review comments as path:line issue lines, branch and head sha, and the instruction to keep every original criterion; same scope, complexity, tier and constraints plus fix_round_for and auto_round = n; inputs = [original, review]; created under the bus lock with the same dedupe key pattern spec reviews use.
3. Reconciliation: in gate() direct-merge and merge_reviewed(), after a task with constraints.fix_round_for merges, set the original task status done, merged_into = the same target, merged_via = 'fix round <fix id> <sha>', hold_reason None; if the original was itself a fix round, walk up the chain.
4. README Pipeline: 'Automatic fix rounds' paragraph with the routine/escalate rule and the round cap; pool.toml [daemon] auto_fix_rounds = 2.
Tests in tests/test_daemon.py: test_auto_fix_round_on_gate_red, test_auto_fix_round_on_review_comments_in_scope, test_no_auto_fix_when_comments_outside_scope, test_no_auto_fix_after_round_cap, test_fix_round_merge_reconciles_original_chain.
acceptance: the generated fix task passes .claude/hooks/require-acceptance.sh (acceptance and scope present) and carries constraints.fix_round_for
README and pool.toml document the rule and the cap
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

spec_review_risks.issue: auto_fix_round() has no coordination with planner_runs.py's existing autonomous 'held' decision point. decision_points() (planner_runs.py:145-152) yields every held execute child unconditionally -- it never checks whether a fix-round task already exists -- so when pool.toml [planner].autonomous=true (the documented executor-container mode), the same tick that has daemon.py deterministically create a fix-round task for a gate_red/in-scope-review hold can also have planner_runs.run() launch a full headless Planner for that same held task, which per CLAUDE.md will itself write another fix-round spec. That produces two competing fix-round branches/spend for one hold and contradicts the invariant merge_reviewed() itself documents at line 610-611 ('a daemon must not invent a spec') without reconciling it. planner_runs.py isn't in scope, but the interaction is unaddressed.

The spec's 'otherwise ... notify once' escalation path names no stamp/dedup mechanism, unlike every other held-notify in this file (dispatch's spec_review_held_at, gate's gated_at, reconcile_dead's orphaned_dirty_worktree), which all wrap notify() in `if stamp(...)`. tick() reruns every interval_s (30s by default); a literal implementation of 'leave hold, notify once' with no persisted marker will call notify() -- an osascript popup plus an optional webhook POST -- every tick for the lifetime of any held task the daemon declines to auto-fix (e.g. a common spec_review request_changes hold). No acceptance test in the list would catch this.

events.reason: superseded by G7 v2 (next G7 task) after spec review T-0293; mark done+merged_into when v2 merges so T-0277 (G8) becomes ready
